capitals.name: Quedlinburg
capitals.note: 'founded on the castle hill of Quedlinburg in the present Saxony-Anhalt in 936'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Quedlinburg row). The page gives the abbey's own site as 90 ha with a 270 ha buffer zone, and no territory; an 8 km circle at 11.15E 51.79N is a soft stand-in. Soltau, Potsdam and Gera (gifts of estates) are not drawn: the page dates no loss for them.
New keyframe: 'In 974 the locality of Duderstadt in south-eastern Lower Saxony was acquired' and the abbey owned it 'for 262 years' (circle 10.25E 51.51N 6 km, soft).
New keyframe: 974 plus the 262 years the page gives is 1236; the page names neither the year nor the taker.

ledger.note: 936: the foundation. The abbey 'was founded on the castle hill of Quedlinburg in the present Saxony-Anhalt in 936' by King Otto I at the request of his mother Queen Mathilda; 'Soltau, 170 kilometres away, given by Otto I in 936'; 'The gifts of Emperor Otto I: 936, 25 estates'.
974: Duderstadt. 'In 974 the locality of Duderstadt in south-eastern Lower Saxony was acquired' (the page names no giver).
About 1236 (page silent on the year and the taker): Duderstadt 'which the abbey owned for 262 years'; 974 plus 262 is 1236.

1802/1803: secularised. 'It was disestablished in 1802/3'; 'the Imperial Abbey was secularized and its territory, properties and subjects were absorbed by the Kingdom of Prussia'. 'Between 1807 and 1813 it belonged to the short-lived French puppet state'.

certainty.note: The page gives only the abbey site and a list of gifts; the circles are stand-ins.

sources.title: Quedlinburg Abbey
sources.note: Founded 936; Soltau 936; Duderstadt 974 (held 262 years); Potsdam 993; Gera 999; Vogte of Weida 1209; disestablished 1802/3; Prussia.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Quedlinburg row.

SCOPE. An abbey of secular canonesses and an Imperial Estate whose abbess 'had a seat and voice at the Imperial Diet'. The page's dated gifts: Soltau 936, the church of Saint Michael 956, Duderstadt 974, Potsdam 3 July 993 (deed of Otto III), Gera 999 ('the provincia of Gera came into the hands of the abbey'; in 1209 'the abbess appointed the Vogte of Weida as administrators of the territory'). Potsdam and Gera are not drawn: the page dates no loss for them, and they would otherwise stay drawn for centuries. 'Later acquisitions totalled more than 150 estates.' The 1802/3 disestablishment is given as two years; 1802 is used (as the Quedlinburg row ends the abbey), with confidence 2. The page's disputes with the Bishops of Halberstadt carry no years.

SHAPES. Quedlinburg 11.15E 51.79N 8 km; Duderstadt 10.25E 51.51N 6 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Duderstadt'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) No territory; (2) the loss of Duderstadt (derived, 1236); (3) the page's end years.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
